solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brush back soiled tiles, most sturdy

indicators.note: says the word for brush is read backwards

parts.note: to brush is to rub

indicators.note: soiled tiles are messed up, so the letters of tiles are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cleaner scrubbing grubby tiles, then oddly praising them as the toughest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUB into BUR; 'soiled' rearranges TILES into LIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Burly means stout and strong, so the superlative is a synonym of most sturdy.

clue.text: Poorly in chest? Expert's needed

indicators.note: the word for poorly goes inside the chest

parts.note: a bin is a box or chest for storage
off means unwell, poorly

explanation.surface: Someone with a chest complaint needs a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly in chest' suggests a medical complaint, but the chest is a storage box. The 's is is.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is British slang for a scientific or technical specialist.

clue.text: Artist trains to obtain that special quality, making masterpiece?

parts.note: RA is Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: the railway takes hold of the quality inside it

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, where trains run
it means that indefinable appeal or charm

explanation.surface: A painter trains to acquire the gift that produces great works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to obtain' is the container signal. 'That special quality' is the indefinable 'it' of charm; the question mark admits a masterpiece is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A great work of art is uncommon, an example of a precious unusual thing.

clue.text: Design stylish portable shelter

parts.note: in means fashionable, stylish
a tent is a shelter you can carry

explanation.surface: Planning a fashionable, carry-around camping shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Design here is purpose or aim, as in by design, a synonym of plan.

clue.text: Fish, with whale initially disappearing below, become calmer

indicators.note: the letter vanishes from the swimmer

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of whale

parts.note: down means below

explanation.surface: A fish loses sight of a whale beneath it and relaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappearing' removes the W ('whale initially') from SWIMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to stop being angry or agitated.

clue.text: Writer might use this current fund, when banking royalty?

indicators.note: the fund sits beside the royalty, as if banking against it

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
K is the abbreviation for king, a royal
a pot is a pool of money

explanation.surface: A financial puzzle about a fashionable investment fund cosying up to the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' means alongside, not depositing money; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-style pen-wielding author dips the nib into this small vessel of ink.

clue.text: Type of diet that's fine in alcoholic surroundings?

indicators.note: the fine letters sit within the next word
the alcoholic word forms the setting around

parts.note: dry means teetotal, so an alcoholic place is non-dry
A1 means first-rate, fine, written AI

explanation.surface: Asking which eating regime is acceptable in a boozy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' signals the container. Fine is A1, written with an I; dry means teetotal, so alcoholic is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Excluding milk products describes a kind of eating plan, as for vegans.

clue.text: Jumble by hospital put in reserve

parts.note: past means by, as in walk by

indicators.note: the hospital letter is placed inside

parts.note: ice is coolness of manner, reserve

explanation.surface: A jumble sale next to a hospital is kept in storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble' is the definition, not an anagram signal; 'put in' is the container signal, and reserve means cool aloofness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche can be a medley or hotchpotch of borrowed bits, a mixture.

clue.text: Gareth excitedly drained prune wine

indicators.note: excitedly means the letters are thrown about
drained means emptied of its middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: Gareth eagerly finishes off his prune wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges GARETH; 'drained' leaves PE from PRUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jokey name for wine, made from grapes.

clue.text: Old marketplaces give out rejects temporarily

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, the marketplace of an ancient Roman town

indicators.note: rejecting sends the word back, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to give out

explanation.surface: Ancient markets handing out their unwanted goods for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' is a verb signalling reversal. Fora is the Latin plural of forum.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means for a limited spell, the same idea as temporarily.

clue.text: Full-body garment from store is enormous — it must be returned

indicators.note: returned means the letters run backwards
the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An oversized all-in-one bought in a shop has to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'storE IS ENOrmous' backwards for the answer; 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an all-in-one leisure suit covering torso, arms and legs.

clue.text: Dignity, regularly with writer, retired together

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of dignity is taken

parts.note: and means with, joining things

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as the writer, me

explanation.surface: An author who has stepped down still keeping their dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes INT from dIgNiTy; 'retired' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in tandem means jointly or side by side, a synonym of together.

clue.text: Comparatively simple puzzle, with time to spend, one cracks

indicators.note: one breaks into the puzzle word
spending the time uses it up, so T goes

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone with time to kill cracks a puzzle that turns out less hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spend' removes T from TEASER, leaving EASER; 'cracks' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of easy means less difficult, simpler than something else.

clue.text: Street band leader in Southall wears check undergarment

parts.note: a ring is a band

indicators.note: the letter is dressed in the check, sitting inside it

parts.note: to vet is to check

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of Southall

explanation.surface: A street band's frontman in Southall, a west London district, wears check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' puts S ('leader in Southall') inside VET.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mesh vest worn under a shirt, an item of underwear.

clue.text: Post of journalist in this period varies

indicators.note: varying the letters changes their order

explanation.surface: Remarks that a newspaper job changes over the course of the current era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varies' rearranges THIS PERIOD; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The position held by the person in charge of a paper's content is this office.

clue.text: Six-pack perhaps taken home, and they endlessly booze

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abs, abdominal muscles
in means at home

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter

explanation.surface: Taking beer cans home so the drinkers can carry on drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-pack' looks like beer but is muscles; 'endlessly' trims THEY to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong aniseed spirit, an example of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Half-sure Elizabethan writer curtailed feature of plot?

indicators.note: half takes the first two letters of sure
curtailed means the tail letter is cut off

parts.note: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan poet

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan author, half-certain, cuts short a storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' gives SU; 'curtailed' cuts the R from SPENSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension about what happens next is a typical element of a thriller's story.

clue.text: Worth playing sport on good floor covering

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: It's worthwhile playing a game on a decent pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges WORTH to THROW; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rug that can be laid anywhere, a loose mat for the floor.

clue.text: Film of the King in sad state

parts.note: blue means sad
Hawaii is a US state

explanation.surface: A movie about a monarch in a miserable condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, who starred in this 1961 film.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a 1961 musical movie starring Elvis Presley, known as the King of rock and roll.

clue.text: Supplies suit sample

parts.note: to fit is to suit
to sup is to sip or sample

explanation.surface: A tailor's offer of goods, with a swatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Equips is the sense: to kit someone out is to provide them with gear.

clue.text: Two businesses operating secure site

parts.note: CO is a company; two of them give CO CO
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A pair of firms running a protected premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A silky casing protecting a pupa is a sheltered, safe place.

clue.text: Ate midday meal? Daughter left out piece of meat

indicators.note: out means these letters are removed

parts.note: had lunch means ate at midday

explanation.surface: After lunch, a daughter left out a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes D and L from HAD LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunch is the leg and loin of an animal as a cut for cooking.

clue.text: Spontaneous performance mostly better

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: to better is to improve

explanation.surface: An ad-libbed show that is largely superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of IMPROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for improvisation, unscripted theatre made up on the spot.

clue.text: General once overturned places in Indian city

indicators.note: places go inside the city

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense this flips the word, so it reads backwards

parts.note: loci are places, the plural of locus

explanation.surface: An old military commander toppling locations in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' makes ICOL from LOCI, which goes 'in' AGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricola was a Roman general who governed Britain in the first century.

clue.text: Chilling territory 'oodlum recalled?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters go in reverse

parts.note: a hoodlum is a hard nut; the dropped H in 'oodlum asks for 'ard nut without its H

explanation.surface: A Cockney thug remembered in an icy land.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe signals a dropped H: hoodlum gives HARD NUT, so 'oodlum gives ARDNUT, reversed by 'recalled'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the treeless frozen plain of the Arctic, cold territory in both senses.

clue.text: Jasmine maybe stirred by such a top one's knitted

indicators.note: knitting works the letters into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A knitter's top is described alongside a fragrant drink being stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' rearranges A TOP ONES. Jasmine is a kind of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon is what one uses to stir a cup of jasmine or other brew.

clue.text: Go from work unit into English city

indicators.note: the unit goes into the other letters

parts.note: NY is New York, the city
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Leaving the office to travel into an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'English city' is not one place but two pieces, the second being New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or drive, as in full of go, a synonym of verve and pep.

clue.text: An easy putt can be shown alongside clubhouse, if really necessary

indicators.note: the second piece sits next to the first

parts.note: a tap-in is a short easy putt in golf
CH is the map abbreviation for clubhouse

explanation.surface: A golfer's short putt shown next to the clubhouse, only when strictly needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an emergency or when nothing better is available.
